title: Fourier, RMS, PEP and converters
blurb: How a square wave is built from sine waves, what RMS and PEP measure, and how analog-to-digital conversion works.

E8A01.why: **Fourier analysis** decomposes a signal into sine waves. A square wave comes out as a sine plus odd harmonics.
E8A01.trap: The other analyses are general maths, not the sine-wave breakdown of a waveform.

E8A02.why: **Successive approximation** is a real ADC method: it homes in on the input value one bit at a time.

E8A03.why: Time domain plots **amplitude against time**, like an oscilloscope. Frequency at each moment is not its job.
E8A03.trap: Showing power or amplitude per frequency is the frequency domain.

E8A04.why: **Dither** is a small deliberate noise added to the input that reduces quantization noise.
E8A04.trap: Dither is not a fault or a decimation method; it is added on purpose.

E8A05.why: A true-RMS meter calculates the heating-equivalent value of **both sine and non-sine waveforms**. Averaging meters assume a sine.

E8A06.why: Speech is peaky, so unprocessed SSB has PEP about **2.5 times** its average power.
E8A06.trap: 1 to 1 is a steady single tone, not speech.

E8A07.why: The ratio comes from **speech characteristics**: brief peaks and quiet gaps. Frequency, carrier suppression and gain do not set it.

E8A08.why: A flash converter compares all levels at once, so its **very high speed** can digitize high frequencies.
E8A08.trap: Flash converters are fast but not low-power.

E8A09.why: N bits give 2^N levels: 2^8 = **256**. Input gain changes the voltage range, not the number of codes.

E8A10.why: The DAC output is stepped. A low-pass filter **removes the sampling artifacts** and leaves the smooth signal.

E8A11.why: ADC quality is judged by **total harmonic distortion**: how much unwanted harmonic content it adds.
E8A11.trap: PEP, reciprocal mixing and power factor belong to transmitters, receivers and AC loads.
